script: Spread and total were not saved for SEA@WAS, so this Seahawks-Commanders script is form-only. Seattle's two games have been Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22 targets, 277 yards, 197 air yards) with a split SEA backfield (Jacardia Price and Emanuel Wilson both 23 carries). Washington has given Jacory Croskey-Merritt the Commanders carry lead (28 carries, 106 yards) while WAS downfield shots have missed (Terry McLaurin 64 yards on 176 air yards, Dyami Brown 21 yards on 112 air yards). The Seahawks have allowed 0 passes of 20-plus on 66 attempts, so the Commanders' path is the run; the Commanders have leaked the middle (13.1 YPA on 10 attempts) and the right (10.46 YPA on 26) while blitzing 43 percent.
who_goes_off: In SEA@WAS, Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba should go off: 138.5 receiving yards a game on 11 targets, into a Commanders defense that has allowed 13.1 YPA in the middle and 10.46 on the right, plus 7 passes of 20-plus on 61 attempts. Commanders back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is the WAS skill player with a path, because the Seahawks have wiped out the explosive pass (0 of 66) and he already leads Washington at 14 carries a game.
weak_spot: The Commanders' leak versus Seattle is the middle (13.1 YPA, 10 attempts) and the right (10.46 YPA, 26 attempts), not the left (3.95 YPA, 20 attempts), so the SEA matchup is slot, nickel, and intermediate right rather than Washington's outside left corner. The Seahawks have no pass soft spot for WAS: left 4.89, middle 4.5, right 4.0, and zero 20-yard passes allowed on 66 attempts. The only relative opening for the Commanders versus Seattle is the run at 3.73 yards per carry, and even that SEA front has allowed just 4 runs of 10-plus.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for SEA@WAS, so there is no Seahawks or Commanders injury fallout to price. The board lists Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota rush yards while the two-game WAS rushing form is Jayden Daniels (12 carries, 100 yards); without an injury note those Daniels rushes are not treated as Mariota's for Washington.
qb_vs_blitz: The Seahawks quarterback is 0.38 EPA per dropback versus the blitz (19 dropbacks) and 0.43 without it, so the Commanders' 43 percent blitz does not knock the Seattle Jaxon Smith-Njigba script off. The Commanders quarterback is -0.10 EPA versus the blitz (20 dropbacks) and 0.23 when unblitzed, but Seattle blitzes only 23 percent, so that WAS weakness is unlikely to be the lever in SEA@WAS.

picks.why: Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 277 yards on 22 targets over two games, 47 yards a game above the 91.5 line, and the Commanders' middle (13.1 YPA) and right (10.46 YPA) are where a 197-air-yard SEA volume receiver lives. Seattle's 0.38 EPA versus blitz means Washington's 43 percent blitz does not take those SEA targets away.

Commanders back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has 28 carries for 106 yards, 53 a game against a 38.5 line. The Seahawks have allowed 0 of 66 passes to go for 20-plus, which pushes WAS toward him, and even at Seattle's 3.73 yards per carry a 14-carry Commanders pace is about 52 yards.
